how: The proposal to surround the displayed figure with further images calls for work on an existing mark.
Praise and accomplishment claims establish recruitment only when a passage also calls for work or reports joining it.
Participants claim a recognisable figure as shared work and report adding another familiar figure.
Status reports keep the standing figure, construction underway, and subsequent stains visible to the thread.
A new-location link and coordinate reply make the returned work findable without establishing an agreed pixel template.
Participants commit to maintenance and prioritise borders, while the added mechanism of uninformed keepers erasing an agreed redesign remains untestable.
The invasion reporter revises the attributed attackers after noticing their writing and acknowledges the earlier translation mistake.
The peace objection resists a war proposal without establishing that it stopped any placements.
References to peace and maintaining borders do not disclose a neighbour's terms or a bilateral negotiation.
War rhetoric answering a background proposal does not distinguish attacking another work from defending the existing figure.
An invasion prompts relocation advice, followed by reported covering, return, and a new location without the detailed move decision.
Participants announce collective accomplishment, recognise the figure, praise the makers, and express pride.
A posterity image, state updates, mourning, and the closing survival report preserve the work's changing condition during and after the event.
Preserving a picture and announcing survival do not show a decision to continue, repurpose, or remake the collective effort.
Fatigue after the return announcement does not establish using scripts, bots, or spare accounts.
The maintenance commitment is a bare one-line follow-up to its author's own proposal rather than evidence of another member joining.
The joke crediting borrowed portals cannot establish help exchanged between actual rooms.
Mentioning a planning chat does not establish a coalition of rooms.
Participants carry the loss in talk through lament, blame, and jokes about the attributed attackers within their own thread.
Maintaining borders does not establish that the work occupied another room's territory under its rules.
A work proposal and a planning chat do not show moderator routing, posting rules, or a decision to contain canvas talk.
The peace objection and border priority state neither disputed authority nor limits on who can commit placers to an agreement.
The direct reply qualifies the survival account by naming remaining damage, matching the revised range of correcting a claim about the work.
A participant locates planning in a chat and brings the selected border priority back to the thread without revealing how the chat decided.
The late confession of incomprehension contains no explicit question or explanation, so it cannot establish the candidate's question-and-explanation process.
The confused speaker does not say the canvas brought them into the room.
Participants make episode-specific jokes from the attacked crab, attributed attackers, and portal rescue rather than only repeating inherited references.
The evidenced new location follows reported covering and does not disclose siting or relocation before any loss.
A collective accomplishment and a named planning chat do not show a room forming around the canvas mark.
Calling attackers jerks does not establish an exchange policing offensive jokes, slurs, or hate symbols.
Imagining pride from a named person does not establish an effort to reach creators or an external audience.
Blaming the covering people does not disclose an exchange arguing whether covering is legitimate or the canvas's point.
Needing sleep does not state withdrawal from the work or a quarrel between members requiring repair.
Translation for attribution and planning in a chat do not establish hiding plans from rivals or entering their venues.
Confusion after the event supplies no evidence of turning against the room's own mark because of canvas posts.
The collective accomplishment claim identifies no member as the first proposer, mapper, or placer even under the revised starter definition.
The returned account of planning identifies no envoy carrying a proposal between rooms.
The accomplishment claim does not establish an April Fools prank frame for the host room.
Fatigue and a new location do not state that too few hands or too little room forced the move.
Naming the attributed attackers does not establish a quarrel predating the canvas.
Familiar figures and sayings make the work recognisable to participants while recognition remains uneven.
Late-night watching and a return announcement explicitly report staying awake and needing sleep as costs of participating.
The closure report establishes that the event ended without describing a site fault or a workaround.
Defending peace does not establish belonging to both rooms in a border dispute.
Volunteering coordination and reporting chat planning establish neither appointed order nor its absence and cannot test the aggregate frequency claim.
The attributed attackers are not linked to a prior tie that explains an attack call.
The visible work proposal follows an accomplishment claim, leaving the original recruitment-to-building mechanism untestable.
The accomplishment claim identifies no starter or sequence in which that starter prompted a call for hands.
The same speaker shows the work appearing and then promises maintenance, supporting the build-to-upkeep transition without identifying individual placements.
Upkeep and a border priority are visible without a disclosed transition to negotiating with neighbours.
The peace objection supplies no settled border terms whose authority then produces restraint.
Loss and tired recovery do not reveal whether strained upkeep led to machine placement.
The return announcement receives explicit celebration of seeing the work again, supporting the transition from reported work to marking accomplishment.
The announcement-to-posterity sequence does not establish that collective celebration motivated preservation.
The preserved image and survival report are not accompanied by a coded decision about future collective activity.
Relocation is reported without a shortage judgement that explains abandoning the earlier spot.
A proposal and later coordinates do not disclose a design argument settled by a shared pixel template.
A speaker's own proposal and commitment cannot demonstrate another reader joining through a call-and-acceptance pair.
The portal-help joke does not establish that strained upkeep produced a request for another room's help.
The border priority and portal joke disclose no negotiated channel later used to trade help.
The work proposal and later war rhetoric do not establish recruited hands turning against a rival's work.
The reasoned peace reply answers war rhetoric but cannot establish an executed attack or an explicit call to deface another work.
Invoking peace does not disclose an attack call followed by bilateral terms or a proposed deal.
The blame answers incoming covering rather than an evidenced attack initiated by this room.
Planning border maintenance in a chat does not establish upkeep producing a coalition.
The visible work proposal supplies no evidence of a subsequent canvas-post flood and host response.
Neither an agreement's terms nor a compliance disclaimer is visible, leaving the newly bounded agreement-to-limit mechanism untestable.
Reported covering is answered by a return announcement and followed by a new-location report without disclosing the causal move decision.
Recovery and relocation return the thread to locating and reporting the work without establishing a causal rebuilding loop.
A post-event statement of incomprehension makes being present a limit on shared understanding without constituting an explicit question or explanation.
Noticing another canvas picture remains a spectator action without requiring questions, explanation, building, recruitment, or helping its makers.
